about: R1 example search mutants, owned by nfa. SearchSkipsImpossibleStarts observes algorithmic work; SearchAgreesWithReferences covers new search semantics not exercised by the original whole-text laws.

mutants.name: R1-literal-machine
mutants.rule: Complete literals need no NFA starts or transitions.

mutants.name: R1-alt-prefix
mutants.rule: Only the common prefix of both alternatives is required.

mutants.name: R1-nullable-prefix
mutants.from:
case Any, Class, Star, Quest:
		Prefix{Text: "", Complete: false}
mutants.rule: An optional head may match empty, so its operand is not required.

mutants.name: R1-overlap
mutants.rule: After a candidate, another prefix may start inside it.

mutants.name: R1-whole
mutants.rule: Whole mode must stay anchored, including complete literals.

mutants.name: R1-early-accept
mutants.rule: Inside accepts before End; trailing bytes cannot undo a match.

mutants.name: R1-no-prefix-fallback
mutants.rule: No required prefix is not evidence of no match; nullable patterns still match.

mutants.name: R1-live-candidate
mutants.rule: Starting a later candidate must preserve earlier live configurations.

mutants.name: R1-cat-incomplete
mutants.rule: A concatenation cannot require bytes after an unknown or variable-length head.

mutants.name: R1-plus-complete
mutants.rule: One required literal occurrence does not make a repeat a complete literal.

mutants.name: R1-rescan
mutants.rule: SearchTransitionsAreLinear rejects redundant suffix rescans that Boolean agreement cannot see; the actual sequential-candidate implementation at bb95113d is also red under this law.
